intent: Business customer (Paul Devlin t/a Devlin Plumbing) asks to refund one of two duplicate £1,096.00 Faster Payment credits to the details his client supplied; agent queried the payer-name difference (A vs M Kowalczyk).
summary: Proceed with the refund as a return-to-source: the refund sort code/account number supplied are identical to the originating account of both credits, and CoP matches "M KOWALCZYK". First check the bank's inbound-payment/recall records for any existing Meridian recall on either credit (to avoid a double return), then set up the £1,096.00 outbound payment for Paul's secure confirmation, and reply explaining the basis, that nothing has been sent yet, and what the bank cannot verify (the holder relationship behind the A/M name difference).

facts.claim: Two Faster Payment credits of £1,096.00 each were received on 21 Sep 09:40 and 22 Sep 14:20 (BST) from payer name text "A KOWALCZYK", Meridian Bank SYN-SC-11-2 / SYN-ACCT-11-2, both with reference "INV 2211 BOILER" and distinct end-to-end IDs MER26092109401201 and MER26092214204811.
The refund destination given by the client and relayed by Paul (SYN-ACCT-11-2 / SYN-SC-11-2, M Kowalczyk) has the same sort code and account number as the originating account of both credits.
Confirmation of Payee on SYN-SC-11-2 / SYN-ACCT-11-2 with name "M Kowalczyk" (personal account) returned matched=true, name at bank "M KOWALCZYK", checked 2026-09-23T10:05:33Z.
The payer name text on the inbound credits ("A KOWALCZYK") differs from the CoP account name ("M KOWALCZYK"); the agent raised this with the customer.
Paul states (customer assertion, unverified by the bank) that Anna is his client, Marek is her husband, the account is Marek's and she uses it; he wants to refund without sending to the wrong place.

The client's text (forwarded by Paul, dated Tue 22 Sep 19:02) asks for one payment to be sent back to the account she paid from; this is a forwarded third-party message, not a bank-verified instruction.

The request is made in the bank's business banking chat by the account holder about his own sole-trader account SYN-SC-11-1 / SYN-ACCT-11-1; no separate verification record is supplied and no refund has been sent.
No recall or return request from Meridian Bank for either credit is recorded in the supplied snapshot (absence of record, not a negative finding).

missing: Whether Meridian Bank has already lodged a recall/return request for either credit (end-to-end IDs MER26092109401201 / MER26092214204811) — needed to avoid returning the same funds twice
Paul's secure confirmation of the outbound £1,096.00 payment to SYN-SC-11-2 / SYN-ACCT-11-2
Independent evidence of who holds the Meridian account or of the Anna/Marek relationship (not obtainable by this bank and not required because the destination is the originating account)

steps.instruction: Check Harrow & Vale Bank's inbound Faster Payment / recall-and-return records for account SYN-SC-11-1 / SYN-ACCT-11-1 for any recall, return request or indemnity claim from Meridian Bank relating to end-to-end IDs MER26092109401201 (21 Sep, £1,096.00) or MER26092214204811 (22 Sep, £1,096.00). Record the result on case 011 before any outbound payment is released.

rationale.explanation: The payer told Paul the duplicate was an app glitch and may also have told her own bank; if Meridian has already lodged a recall, a customer-initiated refund would return the same £1,096.00 twice. This is a material gap specific to the identified credits.
rationale.criterion: Request a named journal lookup only for a material gap; a recall/return request is distinct from a completed return and must not be duplicated

steps.target: Harrow & Vale Bank plc payments/inbound credit records

steps.instruction: Set up, for Paul Devlin's secure confirmation in the business banking channel, one outbound Faster Payment of £1,096.00 from SYN-SC-11-1 / SYN-ACCT-11-1 to sort code SYN-SC-11-2, account SYN-ACCT-11-2, payee name "M Kowalczyk" (CoP matched "M KOWALCZYK" at 2026-09-23T10:05:33Z), reference "REFUND INV 2211 DUPLICATE". Note on the case that this returns the second credit (end-to-end ID MER26092214204811) to its originating account. Release only on Paul's confirmation and only if s1 shows no existing Meridian recall for that credit.

rationale.explanation: The customer is the account holder instructing a payment from his own account; the destination is the exact account both credits originated from and CoP matches, so the 'wrong place' risk he raised is addressed by returning to source. The A/M name difference is unverified but immaterial to a return-to-source. The payment is state-changing and needs his secure authorisation.
rationale.criterion: Identify the exact transaction by reference, amount, date and parties; a customer-authorised outbound payment requires the customer's secure confirmation before release

steps.target: Customer (Paul Devlin) via secure business banking channel

steps.instruction: Reply to Paul in the business banking chat: "Thanks — that helps. The key point is that the details your client gave (SYN-SC-11-2 / SYN-ACCT-11-2) are the same sort code and account number both £1,096 payments came from, and Confirmation of Payee matches 'M KOWALCZYK' on that account. So this would be a return to the account that paid you, not a payment to a new destination. We can't verify who holds that account or confirm the relationship you've described — the payer name on the credits shows 'A KOWALCZYK' — but because it's the originating account, that doesn't block the refund. Nothing has been sent yet. I'm first checking whether the payer's bank has already asked us to return one of the payments, so you don't end up refunding twice. I'll then send you a £1,096.00 payment to those details with reference 'REFUND INV 2211 DUPLICATE' to confirm securely in your business banking; it only goes once you confirm. I can't promise an arrival time. Please keep your client's text and these payment IDs (MER26092109401201, MER26092214204811) for your records."

rationale.explanation: Answers the customer's concern with the evidenced basis (same source account, CoP match), keeps the unverified assertions labelled as such, and states that the payment is pending his confirmation and the recall check rather than implying it has been made.
rationale.criterion: State only the stage the supplied record proves; do not promise arrival times absent an applicable commitment

must_state: The refund sort code and account number are the same account both £1,096.00 credits came from, so the payment would go back to its source
Confirmation of Payee on those details returned a match to "M KOWALCZYK"

The inbound payer name shows "A KOWALCZYK"; the bank cannot verify who holds the Meridian account or the relationship Paul describes — the basis for proceeding is that it is the originating account, not the explanation
Nothing has been sent yet; the payment will only go after Paul confirms it in the secure business banking channel
The bank is checking whether Meridian has already requested a return of one credit before the payment is released, and will not promise an arrival time
Suggested reference "REFUND INV 2211 DUPLICATE" and advice to keep the client's text and the end-to-end IDs for his records
must_not: Claim the Meridian account is joint, is Marek's, or that Anna is authorised on it
Claim the refund has been sent, credited or will arrive by a given time
Claim the name difference has been verified or resolved by the bank
Disclose any detail of the Meridian account beyond the CoP match result already shown
Treat the forwarded text as a verified instruction from the payer
Ask for any PIN, password or one-time code in chat
State that no recall exists; only that none is recorded in the supplied snapshot
